tool_applicability_notes: No promoted RAKL success tool has a validated applicability witness for the NS-R001d projected-remainder bridge.
failure_reuse_notes: DifferenceWitness for F-NS-R001-A1-ENERGY-CRITICALITY: NS-R001d adds Miller's exact strain-space projected advection-plus-quadratic remainder, which A1 did not test; however a snapshot estimate based only on kinetic energy is still exposed to fixed-energy spatial concentration. Cheapest repeat-failure test: evaluate the remainder on one explicit Schwartz divergence-free seed and rescale it with amplitude lambda^(3/2).

DifferenceWitness for F-NS-R001B-LOCAL-GEOMETRY-SCOPE-GAP: NS-R001d replaces pointwise alignment by a nonlocal projected trajectory-motivated quantity. This repairs the local-geometry coordinate but not the snapshot-versus-dynamics gap. Cheapest repeat-failure test: use admissible initial data, not arbitrary histories, and determine whether the dimensionless remainder ratio grows under energy-preserving concentration.
Neither prior failure is a verified impossibility; they are scoped warnings and do not block time-integrated or positive-time Navier-Stokes depletion mechanisms.
unresolved_warnings: A static initial-data falsifier can reject an energy-only snapshot bound but cannot reject an estimate that starts at t>0 and uses actual Navier-Stokes smoothing.
The energy-preserving concentration lambda^(3/2)v(lambda x) is not the Navier-Stokes solution symmetry; it is used only to vary admissible initial data at fixed kinetic energy.
The strain-space projection P_st is nonlocal; the falsifier must bind its conclusion through projection self-adjointness or an exact projected computation, not through an unprojected norm surrogate.
Smallness of the Miller ratio is sufficient only in the theorem's exact regularity setting and is not itself known to follow from finite energy.
